faq.q: How do I start an AI product video?
faq.a: Share the product, paste a public page, or upload a photo. The video agent asks who the clip is for, then returns a script, an actor, and a voice for you to approve.

faq.q: How much detail should I give?
faq.a: Treat it like a short brief to a teammate. Name the product, who it is for, and the one fact the clip must say. More detail makes the first draft closer to the ad you wanted.

faq.q: Can the clip look like a short news item?
faq.a: Yes. Pick a news-style setting, a voice, and the line you want spoken. Set the frame, the language, and the length, then approve the script before it renders.

faq.q: How does the tool use my video brief?
faq.a: Your brief sets the tone, the product, and the platform. The editor writes a script and builds pictures around that line, and you can change either before download.

faq.q: What should a store expect before it picks a video tool?
faq.a: A clear credit price, a file you can use in ads, and a way to change the actor and the script. AIVideosUGC shows the credit cost before the clip starts.

faq.q: What do the voices sound like?
faq.a: You can try a bright voice, a low voice, or a calm one, and hear the line before you commit. Match the voice to the buyer you had in mind for that product.

faq.q: Do I have to install an app first?
faq.a: No. You work in the browser. No extra software is required. Music and captions are available in the same place as the render.

faq.q: Can I generate a video with AI from a product photo?
faq.a: Yes. Pick an AI actor, choose the language and the voice, and the mouth follows the line you approved. You can adjust the delivery before you download.

faq.q: What does my team get from making videos here?
faq.a: A clip without a shoot on the calendar, captions if you want them, and another version when you want to test a second opening. Paid plans include commercial use and no watermark.

faq.q: Are these clips useful in a paid campaign?
faq.a: Yes. Shops run them as the creative in a paid campaign on the networks they already buy. You still approve the claim before the file leaves the account.

faq.q: Can I start a video from a product page URL?
faq.a: Yes. Paste a public product page and the photo on it becomes the product in the clip. You still approve the script and the actor before the render.

faq.q: Can I test two openings of the same product?
faq.a: Yes. Keep the same product photo and make a second opening, a second line, or a second frame. Post the one that fits the buyer.

faq.q: Can the file run as a Facebook or Instagram ad?
faq.a: Yes. Use a square or a tall frame, with an AI actor if the ad needs a face. A Reel or a TikTok cut can use 9:16. The download has no watermark.

faq.q: Can I make ecommerce ads with this AI video generator?
faq.a: One product, one claim, and a frame that fits the placement. The spoken line should match the listing, and the actor should look like the buyer you are paying to reach.

faq.q: Can I choose how the video is rendered?
faq.a: Yes. You choose the AI actor, the voice, the frame, and the length. The credit cost is shown before the render.

faq.q: When can I download the clip?
faq.a: After you approve the script and the voice, the file is ready to download from the editor. A failed render returns the credits for that job.

Starter is $24.50 a month for 200 credits, Pro is $35 for 300, and Premium is $63 for 600. A video spends 24, 40, 60, or 120 credits for 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds. One photo spends 24 credits. You see the number first, and a failed job returns those credits.

definition.title: What Does This AI Video Generator Do?
paras: A shop takes the listing photo and gets a clip a buyer can watch. Nobody on the team has to stand in for that product. Pick an AI actor, clone a voice you have rights to in the languages you sell in, and publish the file to Meta or TikTok.
You can edit the clip before you download it. Choose an AI actor, keep the approved line, and use the language they sell in. Downloads have no watermark, and commercial use is on paid plans.

reasons.h2: Why Shops Use an AI Video Generator
reasons.lead: Spoken product clips, without putting a shoot on the week.

items.t: Match the Voice to the Script
items.d: A shopper can tell when the words and the mouth disagree. The line you approved is the line the face is saying, so the bottle ad does not look dubbed.

items.t: Make Several Cuts From One Photo
items.d: The listing for the insulated bottle can open two different clips. Watch both and post the one that sounds like the brand.
A running shoe aimed at weekend joggers should not use a face from a formalwear ad. Pick the adult actor who could be that jogger.
